messages.subject: Specifying parameters for DIF anaylsis
parts:
Hi all,

I'm running a series of DIF analyses using a graded response model for a 21-item measure with a 7-point Likert scale and ran into a problem. I tested all the items in calibration sample and cross-validation sample, coming away with 17 items and parameters for the focal sample. I fixed the parameters for the focal sample and began testing for DIF in the first comparison sample using the drop method. However, when I got to the step of constraining the slopes and intercepts and freeing the hyperparameters, the model was not identified and the DIF analysis would not run. I am guessing that having no items freely estimated in the focal sample is producing the error? Is there a way to test DIF when the parameters are fixed in the focal sample?

Thanks,
Daniel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Specifying parameters for DIF anaylsis
parts:
The limitation of the DIF() search, especially in the more exploratory scheme you're in, is that it is possible for the scheme to become non-identified without providing anchor items. The next release of mirt actually will throw a warning if it suspects the search will be tending to this problem (among other new features for this function). Your best solution might be to start in the opposite direction via the 'add' schemes, and work your way up from there. It's less efficient in terms of parameter estimates (not necessarily a problem if your sample size is large enough), but shouldn't have this problem occur. HTH.

Phil
